canvas-01.description: The map area of the title sheet of the 1924 Newfield atlas, drawn at 50 feet to an inch in an L shape around the key map, location map, legend and street index, which are not part of the georeferenced area. The long western strip runs along the west side of West Boulevard from north of the borough's built-up area south to Columbia Avenue, taking in block 4 north of Greenwood Avenue and block 5 between Greenwood and Columbia avenues. These are deep, thinly built residential lots fronting West Boulevard, with scattered frame dwellings, a few concrete-block and frame outbuildings, auto houses and sheds, and long open backlands. A heavy line runs along the east side of West Boulevard, marking where the key map begins. South of that line the sheet continues eastward across the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (P.R.R.) right of way, whose tracks and a siding are drawn between West and East Boulevard, to block 6 east of East Boulevard on the north side of Arch. Block 6 is mostly occupied by the Robert Cleeland's Sons rug mill: manufacturing buildings, a cutting room, a dye house, an office and storage building, a warehouse, a boiler or engine room in brick, water tanks of 2,000 and 4,000 gallons and hydrants, with a fire-protection note on watchman, lighting, heat and power, fuel and water supply. A 15 ft alley crosses the block north of the mill, and the land beyond is marked vacant. A dash-and-dot match line with corner letters A and B closes the block on the east, against sheet 5.
notes: Arch is modern Arch Street; East Boulevard here is modern North East Boulevard.
Robert Cleeland's Sons rug mill (Mfg. Rugs) occupies block 6 at East Boulevard and Arch.
Railroad drawn between the boulevards: W. J. & S. R. R. (P. R. R.), today the Vineland Secondary.
The key map (800 ft to an inch), location map, index and legend on this page are outside the mask.

Sheet 1 (title sheet, 50 ft to an inch): the drawn map is the strip west of West Boulevard (blocks 4 and 5: Greenwood Av., Columbia Av.) and, south of the heavy line, the W.J.&S. R.R. corridor and block 6 east of E. Boulevard (Robert Cleeland's Sons rug mill) on Arch. The rest of the page (key map at 800 ft to an inch, location map, index, legend, title cartouche) is masked out. One part.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the western residential district of Newfield at 50 feet to an inch, from Columbia Avenue in the north to beyond Salem Avenue in the south. Three north-south streets cross between them: Oakland, Maple and Colonia Road, drawn slightly askew to the sheet, with long narrow house lots and the blocks numbered 10, 11, 12 and 13. Salem Avenue, 60 ft wide, runs diagonally across the lower part of the sheet towards the business centre to the east. Building is sparse: mostly one- and two-storey frame dwellings with a few in brick or stone, chicken coops, sheds, auto houses, a green house, a storage building with an oil engine, and an auto repairing shop and a hall near the eastern edge on Salem Avenue. On the north side of Columbia Avenue, along the top of the sheet, stand houses and the 1st M.E. Church (heated by furnace, lit by gas), beside a street marked 'not named, not open'. A dash-and-dot line marked as the borough limits crosses the south-west corner. Large parts of block 17 south of Salem Avenue are open land. A compass rose and the scale bar are printed in the open areas, and the eastern margin repeats the edges of the buildings drawn on sheet 3.
notes: Colonia Road is modern Colonial Avenue; Oakland and Maple are modern Oakland Avenue and Maple Avenue.
A street north of Columbia Avenue is marked 'Not named, not open'.
1st M.E. Church on the north side of Columbia Avenue.
50 ft to an inch. Columbia Av., Salem Av., Oakland, Maple, Colonia Rd. (modern Colonial Avenue); 1st M.E. Church; borough limits line. One part.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 shows the business centre of Newfield at 50 feet to an inch. West Boulevard and East Boulevard run north-south either side of the railroad right of way, where the W.J.&S. R.R. (P.R.R. Cape May Division) and the P.R.R. Atlantic City Division separate, with a passenger station between the tracks and a compressor house with electric motors. West of the railroad, along West Boulevard from Columbia Avenue past Salem Avenue, stand stores, a bank, a concrete-block garage, a pool room, an ice house and dwellings. East of the railroad the blocks between Arch, Catawba Avenue, Pearl and Church hold the post office, a bakery, stores, dwellings, a saw mill, wood working shop, lumber and other concrete-block storage buildings, and the Boro Hall with the fire department. South of Pearl are the Newfield Inn, a cement block manufactory, and dwellings along a short north-south street lettered Rena, which turns into the east-west Rena at the bottom of the sheet. Church Street lies at the eastern edge, partly beyond the sheet. Most buildings are frame; a few are brick or concrete block.
notes: Two streets are lettered Rena: the short north-south one between Pearl and Rena is modern Chestnut Street; the east-west one is modern Rena Street.
Arch, Pearl and Church are modern Arch Street, Pearl Street and Church Street; East Boulevard is modern North East Boulevard north of Catawba Avenue and South East Boulevard south of it.
Salem Avenue west of the railroad and Catawba Avenue east of it are one road today.
The junction of Pearl Street with modern South East Boulevard disagreed with the fit by 9.8 m and was rejected.
Post office, bank, passenger station, Newfield Inn, Boro Hall and fire department on this sheet.

50 ft to an inch. Business centre: W. and E. Boulevard either side of the W.J.&S. R.R. (P.R.R. Cape May Divn) and P.R.R. A.C. Divn, Salem Av., Arch, Catawba Av., Pearl, Church, Rena (two streets so named: the north-south one is modern Chestnut Street, the east-west one modern Rena Street). Post office, bank, passenger station, Newfield Inn, Boro Hall and fire department. One part.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the land south of Rena at 50 feet to an inch, south of the business centre. West Boulevard runs down the western edge with a row of dwellings on its west side (the opposite side is marked no exposure), and East Boulevard, marked 'not opened', runs beside it on the east of the main railroad. The W.J. & S. R.R. (P.R.R. Cape May Division) runs straight north-south between the two boulevards, and the P.R.R. Atlantic City Division curves away south-eastwards across the sheet, with a connecting track curving round to the west and a siding to the glass works. Between the lines stand a tool house, a section house, a lumber warehouse with office, a flour and building material shed and the P.R.R. power house in brick. In the south-east is the Durand & Wilcox Glass Co. Inc., marked 'plant not in operation': a lehr house with a melting tank and glory holes, a warehouse, a repair shop in concrete block, a blacksmith shop and a stack, with notes on lighting, heating and watchman service. At the top of the sheet a strip of lots lines the south side of Rena as far as Church, block 24; the rest of the sheet is open land.
notes: Rena is modern Rena Street, Church is modern Church Street.
East Boulevard south of Rena is marked 'not opened'.
Durand & Wilcox Glass Co. Inc., marked 'plant not in operation'.
Only one street junction is drawn (Rena / Church); the sheet is placed from a hand-picked point there and four points carried from sheet 3.

50 ft to an inch. South of Rena: W. and E. Boulevard (E. Boulevard 'not opened'), railroad junction of the W.J.&S. R.R. and P.R.R. A.C. Divn, P.R.R. power house, lumber yard, Durand & Wilcox Glass Co. (plant not in operation). Only one street junction (Rena / Church); placed from that hand-picked point and four points carried from sheet 3.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the eastern part of Newfield at 100 feet to an inch, half the scale of the other sheets. Church runs north-south along the western side, with a jog at Catawba Avenue and again at Pearl, past the R.C. Church. East of it, between Conwell Avenue, Arch and Catawba Avenue, are blocks 9 and 15, with the Baptist Church on Catawba Avenue. Rosemont Avenue runs diagonally north-north-east to Helena, which crosses the top of the sheet. The very large block 8 between Rosemont Avenue, Helena, Madison Avenue and Catawba Avenue is almost empty except for the Edgarton School and a few dwellings. Madison Avenue runs diagonally along the east side. South of Catawba Avenue the blocks between Church, Pearl, Hazel and Rena (blocks 20, 22, 23) are lined with frame dwellings and include the public library. Building throughout is sparse and mostly one- and two-storey frame dwellings with sheds and auto houses. The top-left corner shows pigeon roosts, and the margins carry 'no exposure' notes and the outlines of sheets 1, 3 and 4.
notes: Helena is modern Helena Street, Hazel is modern Hazel Avenue; Church, Arch, Pearl and Rena are modern Church Street, Arch Street, Pearl Street and Rena Street.
Madison Avenue as drawn does not fit its modern line (hand-picked junctions 2 to 6 m off a fit to the other streets, detected ones placed off the drawn street); it was left out of the control.
Hazel is drawn only between Pearl and Rena; modern Hazel Avenue continues north to Helena Street.
Rosemont Avenue crosses Helena with an offset; both junctions are drawn and both were used.
R.C. Church, Baptist Church, Edgarton School and public library on this sheet.
100 ft to an inch. East side: Church, Conwell Av., Arch, Catawba Av., Pearl, Rena, Rosemont Av., Helena, Hazel, Madison Av.; R.C. Church, Baptist Church, Edgarton School, public library. One part.
